text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hairi said: The Arab-Israeli Peace process is very hard and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is withdrawing Israel's commitments towards this process.
-Parliament started its four-day debate of the 1997 state budget with heated discussions.
-Teachers at the state-owned Lebanese University will go on a one-day strike on Friday to protest the government's financial policy towards the university.
-Israeli planes rocketed suspected guerrilla targets in south Lebanon highlands.
-Revenues from real estate taxes increased 25 percent in 1996 to 283.5 Lebanese pounds.
-Middle East Airlines will receive in Paris today one of four leased Airbus planes.
-Pope John Paul II will visit Lebanon after the winter papal nuncio Pablo Puente said.
-The General Labour Confederation demands 500 million Lebanese pounds financial aid from the government.
